analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift excerpts (head lines 1–1202), DaemonState+Coding.swift metadata and its complete patch. The ProviderLoop change is limited to optional connection diagnostics and unauthorized-reconnect bookkeeping at lines 801–810; the coding change adds optional coordinatorConnection decoding (head line 51) and encoding (head line 90). Absent fields remain compatible through decodeIfPresent. These changes alone neither grant serving authorization nor modify encryption, inference admission, cancellation, model verification, cache scoping, billing or add-on/fan authority. No concrete regression is supported by this scope; unchanged surrounding code was not treated as a new issue.
Relevant contracts are connection-bound authorization and revocation (TB-002, TB-011, T-052, T-053), authorization recovery availability (T-057, A-018), and diagnostic exposure/trust accuracy (T-058). Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery and UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery, referenced at ProviderLoop.swift lines 805–810: verify reconnect timing/backoff, drain and connection-generation handling, and that reconnects cannot preserve stale grants or interrupt native retirement. Also examine the CoordinatorConnection definition and state producer/consumer wiring to confirm diagnostics contain no credentials or sensitive evidence and are never used as serving permission. These implementations are outside the supplied evidence; missing source is a coverage limit, not an observed missing control. The selected T-041 details were considered; no cache behavior is changed here.
